At the Highest-Frequency Frontier: Thermal Gravitational Waves from Supernovae Supplemental Material Xun-Jie Xu, Yong Xu, Qiqin Yin This Supplemental Material analytically derives the thermal production rates of gravitons in relativistic and degenerate electron-proton plasma. The analytical results are checked against direct Monte Carlo (MC) integration of the corresponding collision terms. In Fig. S1, we present both analytical and MC results of the GW power spectra for γe− → he− , e+ e− → hγ, e− e− → e− e− h, and e− p → e− ph. As is shown in the figure, our analytical results reach reasonably good agreement with the MC results. The comparison indicates that for semi-quantitative estimate of supernova thermal GW production rates, the analytical formulae presented in this work should suffice. Our code of MC integration is publicly available on GitHub §. 108 1011 1014", "schema": "text", "source": "arXiv"}], "reference": {"misc": ["At the Highest-Frequency Frontier: Thermal Gravitational Waves from Supernovae Supplemental Material Xun-Jie Xu, Yong Xu, Qiqin Yin This Supplemental Material analytically derives the thermal production rates of gravitons in relativistic and degenerate electron-proton plasma. The analytical results are checked against direct Monte Carlo (MC) integration of the corresponding collision terms. In Fig. S1, we present both analytical and MC results of the GW power spectra for γe- → he-, e+ e- → hγ, e- e- → e- e- h, and e- p → e- ph.
